attributes.translation: No matter how beautiful it is, I won't buy a painting that costs millions of yen.
attributes.nuance_translation: A grammar point that highlights that no matter how much (A), the result cannot be avoided.

attributes.body_ja:
「そんな」の項目（こうもく）でも説明（せつめい）しましたが、「こそあど言葉（ことば）」には、「こんな」「そんな」「あんな」や「どんな」などの形（かたち）があります。この文法（ぶんぽう）で使（つか）われている「どんな」は「「どのような」」を短（みじか）くしたものです。この「どんな」に副詞（ふくし）を作（つく）る「に」と「ても」が付（つ）いた「どんなに〜ても」は、「(A) の程度（ていど）がどれくらいでも、(B) の結果（けっか）は変（か）わらない」という意味（いみ）の表現（ひょうげん）です。

「どんなに」は、いろいろな品詞（ひんし）と合（あ）わせることができます。イ形容詞（けいようし）や動詞（どうし）には「ても」、名詞（めいし）やナ形容詞（けいようし）には「でも」を使（つか）います。

「どんなに〜ても」の「どんなに」には、その程度（ていど）や数（かず）がはっきりとわからないという意味（いみ）があります。
attributes.body:
As explained in the そんな grammar point, the こそあど言葉（ことば） may occasionally be seen in the forms こんな, そんな, あんな, or どんな. どんな itself is an abbreviation of どのような, meaning 'in what way', or 'what kind of'. When partnered with に (creating an adverb), and ても, どんなに～ても is used to express the extent of something that is insufficient. It can be translated as 'no matter how (A), (B)'.

どんなに may be attached to any type of word, so long as that word is then followed by でも (in the case of nouns or な-Adjectives) or ても (in the case of い-Adjectives or verbs).

どんなに～ても can literally be translated as 'even if (A) is in however/whatever (way), (B)'.

attributes.source: [AIAIJ] An Integrated Approach to Intermediate Japanese

attributes.description: どんなに vs. いくら + ~ても

attributes.body: Both express 'no matter how', but どんなに〜ても is used with qualities or actions, e.g. どんなに忙しくても行きます ('No matter how busy I am, I'll go'), while いくら〜でも is used with amounts or quantities, e.g. いくら頼んでも無理です ('No matter how much you ask, it's impossible').

どんなに〜ても means 'no matter how' and emphasizes that an outcome remains unchanged even under extreme or difficult conditions, e.g. どんなに努力しても勝てない ('No matter how hard I try, I can't win'). On the other hand, どうしても expresses strong intent or inevitability, often meaning 'no matter what' or 'at any cost', e.g. どうしても行きたい ('I want to go no matter what'). It can reflect either persistence or a lack of alternatives.

Both どんなに〜ても and にしても introduce conditions contrary to results, but with different focuses. どんなに〜ても emphasizes an unchanging outcome despite extreme conditions, e.g. どんなに高くても買います ('I'll buy it no matter how expensive it is'), while にしても is used more flexibly to acknowledge a point while suggesting a contrast or reservation, e.g. 行くにしても、今日は無理だ ('Even if I go, today's not possible').

second_relatable.title: にしても
second_relatable.meaning: Even though, Even if, Even when, Also

attributes.body: Both にも〜ない and どんなに〜ても deal with limitations, but in different ways. どんなに〜ても focuses on the resilience or constancy of an outcome despite extreme efforts or conditions, e.g. どんなに頑張っても無理だった ('No matter how hard I tried, it was impossible'), while にも〜ない expresses helplessness or inability despite intent, often paired with verbs of volition or emotion, e.g. 寝ようにも寝られない ('I can't sleep even if I try').

first_relatable.title: にも～ない
first_relatable.meaning: Cannot... even if one wants or tries, Would like but cannot, Wants or tries but cannot

attributes.body: Both are similar in that they describe doing something 'incidentally' to another action. かたがた is particularly formal and used especially in writing, e.g. お礼かたがたお伺いしたく存じます ('I hope to visit you, in part to thank you.'), while ついでに is far more casual and can be used for even simple daily expressions, e.g. 買い物のついでに郵便局に寄る 'to stop at the post office while going out shopping'.

first_relatable.title: かたがた
first_relatable.meaning: Partly for (the purpose of), In addition to, Along with, By the way, And also to, Incidentally, While
